description: Minimum traffic volume committed by one or both parties under this agreement, expressed in the unit defined by min_volume_unit (e.g., minutes, MB, messages). Triggers true-up billing if actual volume falls below this threshold.
reference: GSMA PRD AA.13; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Unit of measure for the minimum volume commitment (min_volume_commitment_units). MINUTES = voice traffic; MEGABYTES/GIGABYTES = data traffic; MESSAGES = SMS/MMS; ERLANGS = traffic intensity for capacity agreements.

Radio access network generation(s) covered by this agreement. 2G = GSM/GPRS/EDGE; 3G = UMTS/HSPA; 4G_LTE = Long-Term Evolution (LTE); 5G_NR = 5G New Radio (NR); ALL = all generations. Determines applicable IOT tariff tables and NRTRDE reporting scope.
reference: 3GPP TS 22.101; GSMA PRD IR.21; ETSI TS 122 101

description: Scheduled date for the next formal review of this agreement. Triggers workflow notifications to the commercial owner and finance team in advance of the review.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD AA.13

description: Number of calendar days of advance written notice required by either party to terminate the agreement. Governs the termination workflow in contract lifecycle management.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD AA.13

business_glossary_term: Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange (NRTRDE) Flag
description: Indicates whether this agreement requires Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange (NRTRDE) reporting per GSMA PRD FS.11. NRTRDE enables fraud detection by providing near-real-time CDR visibility to the home operator.
reference: GSMA PRD FS.11; GSMA PRD IR.21

business_glossary_term: Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange (NRTRDE) Transmission Window (Hours)
description: Maximum number of hours within which NRTRDE files must be transmitted to the home operator after the roaming CDR is generated. Standard GSMA requirement is 4 hours; some bilateral agreements specify tighter windows.
Duration in months of each automatic renewal cycle when auto_renewal_flag is True. Null when auto-renewal is not applicable.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD AA.13

description: Percentage of gross revenue shared with the counterparty operator under MVNO hosting, content, or wholesale broadband agreements. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 20.00 = 20%). Null for pure IOT/TAP agreements.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD AA.13

description: Direction of roaming traffic covered by this agreement. INBOUND = foreign subscribers roaming on Telecommunication's network; OUTBOUND = Telecommunication's subscribers roaming on the counterparty's network; BILATERAL = both directions.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code used for financial settlement under this agreement (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Governs currency conversion in Amdocs Revenue Management inter-operator billing.
reference: ISO 4217; GSMA PRD AA.13; ITU-T D.150

description: Frequency at which financial settlement is performed between the parties under this agreement. Governs the billing cycle in Amdocs Revenue Management inter-operator invoicing.
reference: GSMA PRD AA.13; TM Forum SID GB922; ITU-T D.150

description: Calendar date on which all parties executed the agreement. May precede the effective_from_date during a transition or notice period. Used for legal and audit trail purposes.

Code identifying the operational system of record from which this agreement record was sourced. AMDOCS = Amdocs Revenue Management; NETCRACKER = Netcracker OSS/BSS; SALESFORCE = Salesforce CRM; SAP = SAP S/4HANA; MANUAL = manually entered.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; TM Forum eTOM

business_glossary_term: Transferred Account Procedure (TAP) File Exchange Flag
description: Indicates whether this agreement mandates Transferred Account Procedure (TAP) file exchange for roaming CDR settlement. True = TAP files must be exchanged per GSMA PRD TD.57 specifications.
reference: GSMA PRD TD.57; GSMA PRD BA.12

description: Version of the GSMA Transferred Account Procedure (TAP) standard used for CDR file exchange under this agreement. Governs file format and field mapping in the TAP processing pipeline.
reference: GSMA PRD TD.57; GSMA PRD BA.12

description: Actual calendar date on which the agreement was terminated, if applicable. Distinct from effective_until_date which is the planned end; this captures early or unilateral termination events.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD AA.13

description: Frequency at which minimum volume commitment true-up calculations are performed. If actual traffic falls below min_volume_commitment_units within the period, a shortfall charge is raised in Amdocs Revenue Management.
reference: GSMA PRD AA.13; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Timestamp when this carrier agreement record was last modified in the data platform. Follows ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Used for change tracking and incremental ETL processing.
reference: ISO 8601; ISO/IEC 27001; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Unique surrogate primary key for the IOT tariff record in the interconnect domain. Serves as the SSOT identifier for wholesale rate lookup during TAP file rating and settlement invoice generation.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: Name or identifier of the business authority (person, team, or system) that approved this IOT tariff record for production use. Required for internal governance and audit compliance in the interconnect settlement process.
The date and time at which this IOT tariff record was formally approved for production use. Part of the tariff lifecycle audit trail. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

The billing increment in seconds used for voice service IOT charge calculation. For example, a value of 60 means charges are calculated per full minute; a value of 1 means per-second billing. Applicable only for voice service types.

The date and time at which this IOT tariff record was first created in the data platform. Serves as the audit creation timestamp for data lineage and compliance purposes. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; ISO/IEC 27001; GDPR Article 5

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the IOT rate is denominated (e.g., EUR, USD, SDR). GSMA IOT rates are typically denominated in EUR or IMF Special Drawing Rights (SDR). Used for settlement invoice currency conversion and financial reconciliation.
reference: ISO 4217; GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: The GSMA-defined or operator-defined destination zone code to which this IOT rate applies. Zones group countries or network destinations for wholesale tariff banding. Used in TAP file rating to match usage records to the correct IOT rate.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA TAP3 Specification; ITU-T E.164

description: Human-readable name of the destination zone (e.g., 'Zone 1 - EU', 'Zone 2 - Rest of World'). Used in settlement reports, finance dashboards, and operator billing correspondence.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Negotiated discount percentage applied to the standard IOT rate under a bilateral roaming agreement. Expressed as a decimal fraction (e.g., 0.1500 = 15% discount). Null if no discount applies. Used in settlement invoice calculation to derive the effective net rate.
reference: GSMA PRD AA.12; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The calendar date from which this IOT tariff version becomes binding and applicable for wholesale roaming charge rating. Aligns with the GSMA IOT effective date published in the inter-operator tariff notification.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: The net IOT rate after applying any negotiated discount_percentage to the standard iot_rate. Stored as a pre-computed field to support high-volume TAP file rating performance. Expressed in the tariff currency per rate_unit.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA TAP3 Specification; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The calendar date on which this IOT tariff version ceases to be applicable. Null indicates an open-ended tariff with no defined expiry. Used to enforce correct rate selection during TAP file rating for a given usage date.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: The exchange rate applied to convert the IOT rate from currency_code to settlement_currency_code for settlement invoice generation. Sourced from the agreed exchange rate mechanism defined in the bilateral roaming agreement (e.g., ECB rate, fixed contractual rate).
reference: GSMA PRD AA.12; ISO 4217; ECB Exchange Rate Reference

description: The GSMA-defined rate group classification for this IOT tariff entry. Rate groups are published in the GSMA IOT rate tables and used to categorise wholesale rates for settlement and benchmarking purposes. Examples: RG1, RG2, RG3 for voice; DG1, DG2 for data.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA PRD IR.21

business_glossary_term: Home Network Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) Code
description: The GSMA-assigned PLMN code (MCC+MNC) of the home operator network for which this IOT tariff is applicable. Enables multi-PLMN operators to maintain separate IOT rate tables per home network entity.
reference: GSMA PLMN List; ITU-T E.212; 3GPP TS 23.003

description: The initial billing period in seconds for voice calls, which may be charged at a different rate or as a flat fee before the standard per-interval rate applies. Common in IOT tariffs where the first 30 or 60 seconds are charged as a connection fee.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; GSMA IOT Specification

description: The IOT rate applied during the initial_duration_seconds period of a voice call, if different from the standard iot_rate. Null if no differentiated initial rate applies. Expressed in the tariff currency.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: Classification of the IOT tariff by commercial arrangement type. 'standard' for GSMA-published rates, 'preferential' for bilaterally negotiated lower rates, 'reciprocal' for symmetric bilateral agreements, 'benchmark' for reference rates used in dispute resolution.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA PRD AA.12; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The date on which this IOT tariff was officially published by the GSMA or notified by the visited operator. Used for audit trail and to verify compliance with GSMA notification lead-time requirements prior to the effective_from_date.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA PRD IR.21

description: The wholesale IOT rate charged by the visited operator to the home operator for the specified service type and destination zone. Expressed in the currency defined by currency_code. For voice: rate per minute; for SMS: rate per message; for data: rate per kilobyte or megabyte as defined by rate_unit. This is the principal quantitative fact of the IOT tariff record.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA TAP3 Specification; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The minimum wholesale charge applicable per usage event under this IOT tariff, expressed in the tariff currency. Ensures a floor charge is applied even for very short calls or minimal data usage. Used in TAP file rating to enforce minimum billing thresholds.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: The reference number or identifier of the official GSMA or bilateral operator notification document that introduced or amended this IOT tariff. Provides an audit trail linking the tariff record to the formal inter-operator communication.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; GSMA PRD IR.21; TM Forum SID GB922

business_glossary_term: Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange (NRTRDE) Eligible Indicator
description: Indicates whether usage records rated under this IOT tariff are subject to NRTRDE near-real-time roaming data exchange reporting to the home operator. True for operators with NRTRDE obligations under GSMA PRD TD.57. Used for fraud detection and real-time roaming cost monitoring.
reference: GSMA PRD TD.57 NRTRDE; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: Indicates whether this IOT tariff applies to peak, off-peak, or flat (time-independent) usage periods. Some bilateral roaming agreements differentiate IOT rates by time-of-day. 'flat' indicates no time-of-day differentiation.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The unit of measure for the IOT rate. Defines the denominator for the iot_rate value. 'per_minute' for voice, 'per_message' for SMS/MMS, 'per_kb' or 'per_mb' for data, 'per_event' for supplementary services. Required for correct TAP file charge calculation.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; GSMA IOT Specification

description: Free-text field for operational notes, special conditions, or exceptions associated with this IOT tariff record. Used by the interconnect team to document bilateral negotiation context, GSMA waiver references, or rate dispute notes.

Classification of the inter-operator roaming agreement under which this IOT tariff applies. 'bilateral' for direct operator-to-operator agreements, 'multilateral' for GSMA-governed multi-party agreements, 'hub' for roaming hub-mediated arrangements, 'mvno' for MVNO wholesale agreements, 'transit' for transit traffic arrangements.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.21; GSMA PRD AA.12; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The rounding method applied to calculated IOT charges during TAP file rating. Governs how fractional charge amounts are rounded to the precision defined by tap_decimal_places. Ensures consistent charge calculation between home and visited operators.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; GSMA BA.12 TAP Data Dictionary

description: Granular classification of the roaming service within the service_type. Examples: MOC (Mobile Originated Call), MTC (Mobile Terminated Call), MO-SMS, MT-SMS, GPRS, VoLTE, 5G NR data. Used for detailed IOT rate differentiation and TAP file reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: moc|mtc|mo_sms|mt_sms|gprs|volte|5g_nr|mms_mo|mms_mt|supplementary — promote to reference product]
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; 3GPP TS 32.240; ITU-T E.164

description: The category of roaming service to which this IOT rate applies. Drives the rating engine selection logic in TAP file processing. Values align with GSMA TAP3 service type codes: voice (MOC/MTC), SMS (MO/MT), data (GPRS/LTE/5G), MMS, and supplementary services.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; 3GPP TS 32.240; TM Forum SID GB922

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code used for the actual financial settlement between operators, which may differ from the IOT rate currency_code. For example, IOT rates may be denominated in EUR but settled in USD per bilateral agreement.
reference: ISO 4217; GSMA PRD AA.12; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: The native primary key or record identifier of this IOT tariff in the originating operational system (e.g., Amdocs Revenue Management tariff ID, Netcracker OSS catalogue ID). Enables traceability from the Silver layer back to the system of record.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; TM Forum eTOM

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this IOT tariff record was sourced or ingested (e.g., 'AMDOCS_RM', 'NETCRACKER_OSS', 'GSMA_PORTAL'). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; TM Forum eTOM

description: The number of decimal places used to express the IOT rate in TAP file records, as defined by the GSMA TAP3 specification. Governs the precision of charge amounts encoded in TAP files exchanged between operators. Typically 5 for most currencies.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; GSMA BA.12 TAP Data Dictionary

description: The GSMA file exchange format type for which this IOT tariff is applicable. TAP3 for standard roaming settlement files, NRTRDE for Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange files used for fraud detection, RAP for Returned Account Procedure files handling billing disputes.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; GSMA PRD TD.57 NRTRDE; GSMA PRD RAP Specification

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this IOT tariff entry within the GSMA/operator tariff catalogue. Used as the business key in TAP file references and inter-operator correspondence.
reference: GSMA IOT Rate Group Specification; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Human-readable descriptive name for the IOT tariff entry, used in settlement reports, operator portals, and finance reconciliation dashboards.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA IOT Specification

description: Current lifecycle state of the IOT tariff record. Controls whether the tariff is eligible for use in TAP file rating and settlement invoice generation. 'superseded' indicates a newer version has replaced this record.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA IOT Specification

description: Version identifier for the IOT tariff record, enabling tracking of rate changes over time. Incremented each time the tariff is revised. Used to ensure TAP file rating applies the correct rate version.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Indicates whether the IOT rate is inclusive of applicable taxes (True) or exclusive of taxes (False). Relevant for operators in jurisdictions where VAT or GST applies to wholesale roaming charges. Impacts settlement invoice tax treatment.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification; ETSI EN 301 908; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC

description: The date and time at which this IOT tariff record was most recently modified in the data platform. Used for change tracking, incremental data loads, and audit compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; ISO/IEC 27001; GDPR Article 5

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the visited network where the roaming subscriber consumed the service. Used to map usage to the correct IOT tariff zone and for regulatory reporting of international roaming charges.
reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; GSMA TAP3 Specification; ITU-T E.164

business_glossary_term: Visited Network Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) Code
description: The GSMA-assigned Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) code (MCC+MNC) of the visited operator network. Used to uniquely identify the roaming partner network for IOT rate lookup and TAP file routing.
reference: GSMA PLMN List; ITU-T E.212; 3GPP TS 23.003

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each Mobile Number Portability (MNP) transaction record in the interconnect domain. Primary key for this entity.
Reference to the inter-operator carrier agreement governing the MNP transaction between Telecommunication and the counterparty operator.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD IR.85

description: Foreign key linking to enterprise.corporate_account. Business justification: Enterprise customers porting number blocks during office relocations or provider changes. Business need: tracking which enterprise account initiated bulk porting requests for service continuity, billi

Foreign key linking to interconnect.interconnect_carrier. Business justification: MNP transaction donor carrier is heavily denormalized with donor_tadig_code, donor_carrier_name, donor_mcc, donor_mnc. Normalizing to interconnect_carrier eliminates all redundancy and provides author

Foreign key linking to network.element. Business justification: Mobile number portability requires HLR/HSS updates to redirect routing. Operations must track which HLR/HSS network element processed each port for audit, troubleshooting, and regulatory compliance. R

Foreign key linking to compliance.mnp_compliance. Business justification: Each porting transaction generates a compliance record tracking SLA adherence, authorization verification, regulatory notification. Essential for porting compliance monitoring, regulatory reporting, a

Foreign key linking to analytics.pipeline_run. Business justification: MNP transactions are processed via porting pipelines. This link enables SLA monitoring (porting duration tracking), supports reprocessing of failed ports, and provides audit trail for regulatory compl

Foreign key linking to partner.partner. Business justification: Number portability transactions often involve partner networks (MVNOs) as recipient operators. Business process: MNP coordination with partner operators, regulatory compliance reporting, partner opera

The Port Authorisation Code (PAC) or equivalent subscriber-provided authorisation token used to validate the subscriber's consent for the port-out. Mandatory in many regulatory frameworks (e.g., Ofcom PAC regime, FCC subscriber verification). Null for port-in transactions where PAC is consumed by the gaining operator.
reference: Ofcom General Conditions C8; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; BEREC MNP Guidelines

description: Reference to the batch file or TAP/NRTRDE file submission in which this MNP transaction was included for inter-operator exchange or regulatory reporting. Supports reconciliation with interconnect file processing workflows.
reference: GSMA PRD TD.57 (TAP3); GSMA PRD IR.85; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Free-text description of the reason the MNP request was cancelled. Populated only when port_status = 'cancelled'. Common reasons include subscriber withdrawal, duplicate request cancellation, or operator-initiated cancellation.
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The actual date and time when the number portability transfer was successfully completed and the MSISDN became active on the recipient network. Null if the port has not yet completed.
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; TM Forum SID GB922

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction in which the MNP transaction is executed. Determines the applicable regulatory framework (FCC, Ofcom, BEREC NRA, etc.) and porting timeline obligations.
reference: ISO 3166-1; ITU-T E.164; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; BEREC MNP Guidelines

description: The date and time when this MNP transaction record was first created in the system of record (Oracle Communications Order and Service Management / Netcracker OSS). Audit trail field for data lineage.

Result of the fraud prevention check performed on the MNP request. 'not_checked' — fraud screening not yet performed; 'passed' — no fraud indicators detected; 'flagged' — suspicious activity detected, under review; 'blocked' — request blocked due to confirmed fraud. Supports GSMA fraud prevention guidelines.
reference: GSMA PRD FS.11; GSMA PRD IR.85; ISO/IEC 27001; FCC 47 CFR Part 64

business_glossary_term: Home Location Register / Home Subscriber Server (HLR/HSS) Update Status
description: Status of the HLR (2G/3G) or HSS/UDM (4G/5G) subscriber profile update triggered by the MNP transaction. 'pending' — update not yet sent; 'completed' — subscriber profile successfully updated; 'failed' — update failed, requiring manual intervention.
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; 3GPP TS 29.272; Ericsson Network Manager; Nokia NetAct

description: The Integrated Circuit Card Identifier of the SIM card associated with the MSISDN at the time of the porting request. Captured to support SIM swap validation and fraud prevention during the MNP process.
reference: ITU-T E.118; 3GPP TS 22.042; GSMA SGP.02; ISO/IEC 7812

description: The International Mobile Subscriber Identity associated with the subscriber's SIM at the time of the porting request. Used for HLR/HSS deprovisioning on port-out and provisioning on port-in. Constitutes PII as it uniquely identifies a subscriber.
reference: ITU-T E.212; 3GPP TS 23.003; GSMA PRD IR.21; GDPR Article 4

description: Indicates whether an inter-operator charge (IOT) is applicable for this MNP transaction under the governing carrier agreement. True = charge applies and will be raised in settlement; False = no charge applicable (e.g., regulatory zero-rating or waiver).
reference: GSMA PRD IR.85; TM Forum SID GB922; ITU-T D-Series Recommendations

business_glossary_term: Mobile Station International Subscriber Directory Number (MSISDN)
description: The full E.164-formatted mobile phone number being ported. This is the subscriber's publicly dialable number and constitutes PII as it directly identifies an individual subscriber.
reference: ITU-T E.164; 3GPP TS 23.003; GDPR Article 4; FCC 47 CFR Part 52

description: The radio access network generation (2G/3G/4G/5G) on which the subscriber's service is provisioned at the time of the MNP transaction. Relevant for HLR vs HSS/UDM routing update determination and network-specific porting procedures.
reference: 3GPP TS 22.011; 3GPP TS 23.116; ETSI; TM Forum SID GB922

business_glossary_term: Number Portability Administration Centre (NPAC) Order ID
description: The order identifier assigned by the Number Portability Administration Centre (NPAC) or equivalent national clearinghouse system (e.g., Syniverse, CODA) for this porting transaction. Used for cross-system reconciliation and regulatory audit.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 52; GSMA PRD IR.85; NTIA

description: The operator or entity that holds the ITU/national regulatory authority allocation of the number range (NXX or equivalent) containing the ported MSISDN. May differ from the donor operator in MVNO or wholesale scenarios.
reference: ITU-T E.164; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; Ofcom National Telephone Numbering Plan; NTIA

description: The order reference number from Oracle Communications Order and Service Management (OSM) or Netcracker OSS/BSS that orchestrated the service fulfillment actions associated with this MNP transaction (e.g., HLR/HSS update, service deprovisioning/provisioning).
reference: Oracle Communications OSM; TM Forum eTOM; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this MNP porting request by the Number Portability Administration Centre (NPAC) or equivalent national clearinghouse. Used for cross-operator tracking and regulatory audit.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 52; GSMA PRD IR.85; ITU-T E.164

description: Current lifecycle status of the MNP transaction. 'pending' — request received and awaiting validation; 'validated' — subscriber eligibility confirmed; 'completed' — number successfully ported; 'rejected' — request denied (see rejection_reason); 'cancelled' — request withdrawn before completion.
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; TM Forum SID GB922; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; BEREC MNP Guidelines

description: Indicates the direction of the number portability event from Telecommunication's perspective. 'port_in' means the subscriber is moving their number to Telecommunication from another operator (donor). 'port_out' means the subscriber is leaving Telecommunication to another operator (recipient).
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD IR.85

description: The elapsed time in hours between request_timestamp and completion_timestamp. Used for SLA compliance monitoring against regulatory maximum porting time mandates (e.g., FCC 1-business-day rule, Ofcom 1-working-day rule). Null if port not yet completed.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 52; Ofcom General Conditions; BEREC MNP Guidelines

description: The scheduled end date and time of the porting window. If the port is not completed within this window, the transaction may expire or require rescheduling per regulatory requirements.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 52; Ofcom General Conditions; BEREC MNP Guidelines; 3GPP TS 23.116

description: The scheduled start date and time of the porting window during which the number transfer is authorised to execute. Regulatory frameworks (e.g., FCC, Ofcom) mandate specific porting windows.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 52; Ofcom General Conditions; BEREC MNP Guidelines; 3GPP TS 23.116

description: Human-readable commercial name of the recipient (gaining) operator. Complements recipient_tadig_code for reporting and business user readability.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.85; TM Forum SID GB922

business_glossary_term: Recipient Network Transferred Account Data Interchange Group (TADIG) Code
description: The GSMA TADIG code identifying the recipient (gaining) operator network to which the MSISDN is being ported. Complements donor_tadig_code to fully describe the inter-operator porting pair.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.21; GSMA TADIG Code Registry; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The latest permissible timestamp by which the MNP transaction must be completed under applicable regulatory rules (e.g., FCC 1-business-day, Ofcom 1-working-day). Used for SLA breach detection and regulatory compliance monitoring.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 52; Ofcom General Conditions; BEREC MNP Guidelines; NTIA

description: The official reference number assigned by the national regulatory authority (e.g., FCC, Ofcom, BEREC member NRA) or Number Portability Administration Centre (NPAC) for this porting transaction. Required for regulatory audit and compliance reporting.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 52; Ofcom General Conditions; BEREC MNP Guidelines; NTIA

description: Standardised code indicating why the MNP request was rejected. Common codes include: MSISDN_NOT_FOUND, OUTSTANDING_BALANCE, ACTIVE_CONTRACT, INVALID_ACCOUNT_HOLDER, DUPLICATE_REQUEST, REGULATORY_HOLD. Populated only when port_status = 'rejected'. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MSISDN_NOT_FOUND|OUTSTANDING_BALANCE|ACTIVE_CONTRACT|INVALID_ACCOUNT_HOLDER|DUPLICATE_REQUEST|REGULATORY_HOLD|FRAUD_SUSPECTED|TECHNICAL_ERROR — promote to reference product]
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; GSMA PRD IR.85; BEREC MNP Guidelines

description: Free-text narrative description of the rejection reason, providing additional context beyond the rejection_reason_code. Populated only when port_status = 'rejected'. Used for dispute resolution and regulatory reporting.
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The date and time when the MNP porting request was formally submitted by the subscriber or the gaining operator. This is the principal business event timestamp marking the start of the porting lifecycle.
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; FCC 47 CFR Part 52; GSMA PRD IR.85

description: The number of times this MNP transaction has been retried following a failure or rejection. Used for operational monitoring, SLA tracking, and identifying systemic porting issues with specific operators.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; TM Forum eTOM

description: The routing number (RN) assigned to the ported MSISDN in the Number Portability database, used by all operators to correctly route calls and SMS to the ported number on the recipient network. Aligned with ITU-T E.164 routing principles.
reference: ITU-T E.164; 3GPP TS 23.116; GSMA PRD IR.85; FCC 47 CFR Part 52

description: Indicates whether the routing number in the Number Portability database and HLR/HSS/UDM has been successfully updated following port completion. 'pending' — update queued; 'updated' — successfully propagated; 'failed' — update error requiring intervention; 'not_required' — no routing change needed.
reference: 3GPP TS 23.116; 3GPP TS 23.003; TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD IR.85

description: Classification of the subscriber service type associated with the porting MSISDN. Determines applicable porting rules, timelines, and regulatory obligations. 'mvno' indicates the subscriber is on a Mobile Virtual Network Operator (MVNO) arrangement.
reference: 3GPP TS 22.011; TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD IR.85; FCC 47 CFR Part 52

description: The monetary amount charged or credited between Telecommunication and the counterparty operator for this MNP transaction under the applicable inter-operator tariff (IOT). Expressed in the settlement currency defined in the carrier agreement. Null if inter_operator_charge_applicable = False.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.85; TM Forum SID GB922; ITU-T D-Series Recommendations

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the currency in which the inter-operator settlement amount for this MNP transaction is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Must align with the settlement currency in the governing carrier agreement.
reference: ISO 4217; GSMA PRD IR.85; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Indicates whether this MNP transaction exceeded the regulatory or contractual maximum porting time SLA. True = SLA breached; False = within SLA. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and inter-operator dispute management.
reference: FCC 47 CFR Part 52; Ofcom General Conditions; BEREC MNP Guidelines; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Local time (HH:MM, 24-hour format) at which the peak rate period begins each weekday. Used by the rating engine to determine which rate tier applies to a given CDR based on call start time.

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this rate entry within the wholesale rate schedule. Used in TAP file references and inter-operator billing reconciliation.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: Human-readable descriptive name for the rate entry (e.g., 'US Domestic Voice Termination Peak', 'EU Roam-Like-At-Home SMS'). Used in rate schedule documentation and commercial negotiations.

Current lifecycle state of the rate record: active (currently in force for rating), pending (approved but not yet effective), superseded (replaced by a newer rate version), expired (past effective period), or withdrawn (cancelled before activation). Controls whether the rate is used in CDR rating and settlement.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; Amdocs Revenue Management Rate Table Lifecycle

description: Classification of the rate by traffic direction and role: termination (delivering traffic to destination network), origination (collecting traffic from originating network), transit (passing traffic through an intermediate network), transit_international (cross-border transit), or access (local loop access charge). Governs regulatory framework applicability.
reference: FCC Part 51 Access Charge Rules; Ofcom FAMR; BEREC Guidelines on Interconnection

description: Maximum rate permitted by the applicable regulatory framework for this service type and destination (e.g., EU RLAH wholesale voice cap of €0.032/min, Ofcom FAMR charge control ceiling). The actual rate must not exceed this cap. Used for compliance validation and regulatory reporting.
reference: EU Regulation 531/2012 (RLAH); Ofcom FAMR 2021; FCC Part 51; BEREC BoR (22) 137

description: Identifier or citation of the specific regulatory instrument governing this rate (e.g., 'FCC Part 51 Access Charges', 'Ofcom FAMR 2021 Charge Control', 'EU Regulation 531/2012 RLAH Cap', 'BEREC Roaming Guidelines'). Enables compliance traceability and regulatory reporting.
reference: FCC Part 51; Ofcom FAMR 2021; EU Regulation 531/2012; BEREC BoR (22) 137; ITU-T D.150

description: Duration increment in seconds to which call durations are rounded up for billing purposes (e.g., 6-second or 60-second rounding). Directly impacts settlement amounts and must align with the counterparty carrier agreement terms.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.85; TM Forum SID GB922; FCC Part 51

description: Type of telecommunications service to which this rate applies: voice (per-minute voice call termination/origination), sms (short message service per-event), data (per-kilobyte or per-megabyte data transit), mms (multimedia messaging), or premium_sms (premium-rate short message service). Determines the billing unit and regulatory regime.
reference: 3GPP TS 32.240; TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD IR.85

description: Name of the operational system of record from which this rate was ingested (e.g., 'Amdocs Revenue Management', 'Netcracker OSS/BSS', 'Manual Upload'). Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation between source systems and the lakehouse.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Lineage Standards

description: TAP file rate category code as defined in the GSMA Transferred Account Procedure (TAP3) specification. Maps this rate to the correct TAP record type for inter-operator roaming settlement file generation and validation.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification (TD.57); GSMA PRD IR.21

description: IANA time zone identifier (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London') used to interpret peak/off-peak/weekend time boundaries for this rate. Ensures correct tier selection across geographic regions and daylight saving transitions.
reference: IANA Time Zone Database; ITU-T E.164

description: Indicates whether this rate applies to inbound traffic (received from the counterparty carrier), outbound traffic (sent to the counterparty carrier), or bilateral (symmetric rate applicable in both directions). Critical for settlement calculation and IOT tariff alignment.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: Unit of measure against which the rate is applied for billing purposes: per_minute or per_second for voice, per_event for SMS/MMS, per_mb/per_kb/per_gb for data. Determines how CDR volumes are multiplied by the rate to produce settlement charges.
reference: 3GPP TS 32.240; GSMA TAP3 Specification; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Sequential version number of this rate record, incremented each time the rate is amended. Enables rate history tracking and ensures the correct version is applied to CDRs within a given effective period. Version 1 is the initial rate.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; Amdocs Revenue Management Rate Versioning

description: Minimum traffic volume (in the rate_unit) at which a tiered or volume-discount rate becomes applicable. Null for flat-rate structures. Used by the rating engine to select the correct rate tier based on cumulative monthly traffic volumes.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; Amdocs Revenue Management

description: Per-unit wholesale charge applied during weekend periods (Saturday and Sunday). May differ from both peak and off-peak weekday rates. Expressed in settlement currency per billing unit.
reference: FCC Part 51; Ofcom FAMR 2021; TM Forum SID GB922

business_glossary_term: Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange (NRTRDE) Record ID
description: Unique surrogate identifier for each NRTRDE event record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
Reference to the bilateral roaming agreement governing this traffic exchange between the visited and home operators. Determines applicable Inter-Operator Tariff (IOT) rates and settlement terms.
reference: GSMA PRD AA.12 Roaming Agreement; TM Forum SID

description: Identifier of the radio cell in the visited network where the roaming subscriber was served. Used for network-level fraud detection (e.g., impossible travel analysis) and geographic usage pattern analysis.

Foreign key linking to interconnect.iot_tariff. Business justification: NRTRDE record currently references IOT tariff via string iot_tariff_code. Normalizing to iot_tariff enables proper rate validation and settlement tracking. The FK will be populated during NRTRDE proce

Foreign key linking to inventory.ont_asset. Business justification: Near-real-time roaming data exchange for FWA services must link to specific ONT assets for immediate fraud alerts and high-usage threshold monitoring. Critical for real-time revenue assurance on fixed

Foreign key linking to analytics.pipeline_run. Business justification: NRTRDE records are ingested via ETL pipelines. This link supports data quality monitoring, SLA breach analysis (transmission latency), and reprocessing workflows when NRTRDE validation fails or reconc

Foreign key linking to compliance.privacy_consent. Business justification: NRTRDE records contain near-real-time subscriber data requiring consent for processing and sharing with roaming partners. Essential for consent validation in real-time data exchange and GDPR complianc
Reference to the TAP file that this NRTRDE record will ultimately reconcile against during post-event settlement. Links pre-TAP roaming visibility to the formal TAP billing cycle.
reference: GSMA TD.57 TAP3 Standard; GSMA BA.40

description: Foreign key linking to interconnect.interconnect_carrier. Business justification: NRTRDE record visited carrier is denormalized via visited_tadig, visited_plmn_id, visited_country_code. Normalizing to interconnect_carrier eliminates redundancy and provides authoritative carrier mas

Access Point Name used by the roaming subscriber for the data session, identifying the packet data network gateway and service type (e.g., internet, IMS, enterprise VPN). Applicable for DATA record types. Used for data service classification and IOT tariff selection.

Sequential number of the NRTRDE transmission batch (file) from the visited operator, used to detect missing batches and ensure complete data receipt. Increments with each new file transmission per GSMA BA.40 batch numbering rules.

Duration of the voice call or supplementary service event in seconds, as reported by the visited network. Applicable for VOICE and SUPPLEMENTARY record types. Used for IOT charge calculation and revenue assurance validation.
reference: GSMA BA.40; GSMA TD.57 TAP3; 3GPP TS 32.250

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the estimated IOT charge is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency settlement reconciliation between international operators.
reference: ISO 4217; GSMA BA.40; GSMA PRD AA.14

description: Monetary difference between the estimated IOT charge in this NRTRDE record and the final charge confirmed in the reconciled TAP file. Populated after TAP reconciliation. Positive value indicates NRTRDE overestimated; negative indicates underestimation. Used for revenue assurance leakage analysis.
reference: GSMA BA.40; GSMA TD.57 TAP3; TM Forum Revenue Assurance Guidelines

description: Date and time (UTC) when this NRTRDE record was first ingested and created in the Silver layer lakehouse. Audit trail field for data lineage and processing SLA measurement.
reference: TM Forum Data Management Guidelines; ISO/IEC 27001

description: Volume of data transmitted from the network to the roaming subscriber's device (downlink) in kilobytes during a GPRS/data session. Applicable for DATA record types. Used for IOT data charge calculation.
reference: GSMA BA.40; GSMA TD.57 TAP3; 3GPP TS 32.251

description: Volume of data transmitted from the roaming subscriber's device to the network (uplink) in kilobytes during a GPRS/data session. Applicable for DATA record types. Used for IOT data charge calculation.
reference: GSMA BA.40; GSMA TD.57 TAP3; 3GPP TS 32.251

description: The destination number dialed by the roaming subscriber for voice calls (B-party number in E.164 format). Applicable for MOC record types. Used for fraud detection (e.g., premium rate number abuse, international revenue share fraud) and traffic analysis.
reference: ITU-T E.164; 3GPP TS 32.250; GSMA PRD FS.11

description: Estimated wholesale charge for this roaming event calculated by the visited network using the applicable IOT tariff at time of NRTRDE transmission. This is a pre-settlement estimate; the final charge is confirmed in the TAP file. Used for early revenue assurance and cash flow forecasting.
reference: GSMA BA.40; GSMA PRD AA.14 IOT; TM Forum SID

description: Calendar date (UTC) on which the roaming service event occurred, derived from service_start_timestamp. Used as a partition key in the Silver layer lakehouse for efficient time-range queries and daily revenue assurance reporting.
reference: GSMA BA.40; TM Forum Lakehouse Architecture

description: Flag indicating that this NRTRDE record has triggered a fraud alert to the Revenue Assurance domain based on anomalous usage patterns (e.g., impossible travel, velocity breach, SIM cloning signatures). True = fraud alert raised; False = no alert.
reference: GSMA PRD FS.11 Fraud Information Gathering System (FIGS); GSMA BA.40

description: Flag set by the visited network indicating that this subscriber's cumulative roaming usage has exceeded a predefined high-usage threshold, triggering potential fraud alert or credit limit notification to the home operator per GSMA BA.40 high-usage detection rules.
reference: GSMA BA.40 NRTRDE Standard; GSMA PRD FS.11 Fraud

business_glossary_term: Home Network Transferred Account Data Interchange Group (TADIG) Code
description: 5-character GSMA TADIG code identifying the subscriber's home network operator. Used to route NRTRDE records to the correct home PLMN for revenue assurance and fraud detection.
reference: GSMA TADIG Code Registry; GSMA BA.40; ITU-T E.212

description: 15-digit unique identifier of the mobile device used during the roaming event. Used for device-level fraud detection (e.g., blacklisted IMEI, IMEI/IMSI mismatch indicating SIM cloning) and equipment analytics.
reference: GSMA IMEI Database; 3GPP TS 23.003; GSMA PRD FS.11

description: 15-digit globally unique identifier assigned to the subscriber's SIM card, used to identify the roaming subscriber across visited and home networks. Classified as restricted PII as it directly identifies an individual subscriber.

Location Area Code identifying the geographic area within the visited network where the roaming event occurred. Used alongside Cell ID for subscriber location tracking and fraud detection in the interconnect domain.

business_glossary_term: Mobile Station International Subscriber Directory Number (MSISDN)
description: The subscriber's mobile phone number in E.164 format, representing the dialable number associated with the roaming event. Classified as restricted PII as it directly identifies an individual.

Radio access technology generation used to deliver the roaming service. Values: 2G (GSM/GPRS/EDGE), 3G (UMTS/HSPA), 4G_LTE (Long-Term Evolution), 5G_NR (5G New Radio), WIFI (Wi-Fi calling/VoWiFi). Impacts IOT tariff applicability and fraud pattern analysis.

Version of the GSMA BA.40 NRTRDE standard used to generate this record (e.g., 2.0, 3.0). Required for backward-compatible processing as operators may transmit records under different standard versions during migration periods.

Current lifecycle state of the NRTRDE record within the interconnect operations processing pipeline. RECEIVED=ingested from visited network; VALIDATED=passed format/content checks; ENRICHED=IOT tariff and agreement data applied; RECONCILED=matched to TAP file; REJECTED=failed validation; DISPUTED=charge under dispute.
reference: GSMA BA.40; TM Forum eTOM Process Framework

description: Specific CDR record type classifying the direction and nature of the roaming event. MOC=Mobile Originated Call, MTC=Mobile Terminated Call, GPRS=data session, SMS_MO=outbound SMS, SMS_MT=inbound SMS. Aligns with TAP3 record type taxonomy.
reference: GSMA TD.57 TAP3; 3GPP TS 32.250; GSMA BA.40

description: Standardized code indicating the reason a NRTRDE record was rejected during validation processing (e.g., invalid IMSI format, unknown TADIG, missing mandatory field, duplicate sequence number). Populated only when processing_status = REJECTED. Aligns with GSMA TAP error code taxonomy.
reference: GSMA TD.57 TAP3 Error Codes; GSMA BA.40

description: Indicates whether this roaming event is inbound (foreign subscriber roaming on our network — we are the visited operator) or outbound (our subscriber roaming on a foreign network — we are the home operator). Determines revenue assurance treatment and settlement flow.
reference: GSMA BA.40; GSMA PRD AA.12; TM Forum SID

description: Sequential number assigned to the NRTRDE record within a transmission batch, used to detect gaps, duplicates, and ordering issues during inter-operator exchange per GSMA BA.40.

The exact date and time (UTC) when the roaming service event concluded. For voice calls this is call release time; for data sessions this is PDP context deactivation. Used to derive call/session duration and validate against usage volume.

The exact date and time (UTC) when the roaming service event began — the principal real-world event time. For voice calls this is call answer time; for data sessions this is PDP context activation; for SMS this is submission time. Core field for NRTRDE 4-hour transmission SLA compliance measurement per GSMA BA.40.

Category of telecommunications service consumed during the roaming event. Drives IOT tariff selection, usage volume interpretation, and revenue assurance thresholds. Values: VOICE (voice call), SMS (short message), DATA (packet data), MMS (multimedia message), SUPPLEMENTARY (supplementary services).
reference: GSMA BA.40; 3GPP TS 32.250; TM Forum SID

description: Flag indicating whether this NRTRDE record was transmitted outside the GSMA BA.40 4-hour SLA window (transmission_latency_minutes > 240). True = SLA breached; False = within SLA. Used for inter-operator SLA performance reporting and penalty calculation.

Name of the NRTRDE transmission file from which this record was extracted, following GSMA BA.40 file naming conventions. Used for batch traceability, reprocessing, and audit trail in the interconnect operations pipeline.
reference: GSMA BA.40 NRTRDE Standard; TM Forum Data Lineage

description: Status of reconciliation between this NRTRDE pre-TAP record and the corresponding TAP3 billing record. PENDING=TAP file not yet received; MATCHED=successfully reconciled; UNMATCHED=no corresponding TAP record found; PARTIAL=partial match with charge discrepancy. Critical for revenue assurance.
reference: GSMA TD.57 TAP3; GSMA BA.40; TM Forum Revenue Assurance

description: Elapsed time in minutes between service_start_timestamp and transmission_timestamp. Measures compliance with the GSMA BA.40 4-hour (240-minute) near-real-time transmission SLA. Records exceeding 240 minutes are flagged for SLA breach reporting.

Date and time (UTC) when the NRTRDE record was transmitted by the visited network to the home network. Used to calculate transmission latency against the GSMA BA.40 4-hour SLA requirement from service delivery.

Date and time (UTC) when this NRTRDE record was last modified in the Silver layer lakehouse, such as after TAP reconciliation, status update, or fraud flag enrichment. Audit trail field for data lineage.
reference: TM Forum Data Management Guidelines; ISO/IEC 27001

business_glossary_term: Return of Accounting Procedure (RAP) File ID
description: Unique surrogate identifier for the RAP file record in the interconnect settlement system. Primary key for the rap_file data product.
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; TM Forum SID

description: Reference to the bilateral roaming agreement under which the rejected TAP records were exchanged. Links the RAP file to the governing commercial and technical terms for the inter-operator relationship.
reference: GSMA BA.08; TM Forum SID; ITU-T D.150

description: Reference to the IOT tariff table applicable to the rejected TAP records. Used to validate whether the rejection relates to tariff mismatches and to recalculate correct charges upon resubmission.
reference: GSMA BA.08; ITU-T D.150; TM Forum SID

description: Foreign key linking to analytics.pipeline_run. Business justification: RAP file processing is an ETL workflow. This link enables monitoring of rejection file handling, supports resubmission workflows when TAP files are rejected, and provides audit trail for dispute resol

business_glossary_term: Resubmission Transferred Account Procedure (TAP) File ID
description: Reference to the corrected TAP file resubmitted by the sender after processing this RAP rejection. Tracks the correction lifecycle and links the original rejection to its resolution.
reference: GSMA TD.32; GSMA BA.08; TM Forum eTOM

description: Foreign key linking to interconnect.interconnect_carrier. Business justification: RAP file sender is denormalized via sender_tadig. Normalizing to interconnect_carrier provides authoritative carrier master reference. The FK will be populated at RAP file creation when sender is know

business_glossary_term: Source Transferred Account Procedure (TAP) File ID
description: Reference to the originating TAP file whose records are being rejected in this RAP file. Links the RAP rejection back to the specific TAP file that contained the erroneous records.
reference: GSMA PRD TD.57; GSMA BA.08; TM Forum SID

description: Date and time when the recipient operator formally acknowledged receipt and acceptance of this RAP file. Required for GSMA bilateral exchange compliance and settlement audit.

Identifier of the GSMA-accredited data clearing house (DCH) or billing clearing house (BCH) that processed or routed this RAP file between operators (e.g., SYNIVERSE, HROAMING). Required for multi-lateral settlement audit.
reference: GSMA PRD TD.57; GSMA BA.08; ITU-T D.150

description: Date and time when the RAP file was generated by the sending operator's settlement system. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this RAP file record.
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; GSMA BA.08

description: Reference number of any formal inter-operator dispute raised in connection with this RAP file rejection. Links the RAP record to the dispute management workflow in the BSS settlement system.
reference: GSMA BA.08; TM Forum eTOM; Amdocs Revenue Management

description: Foreign exchange rate applied to convert the rejected charge amounts from the TAP file currency to the settlement currency at the time of RAP file generation. Required for multi-currency settlement reconciliation.
Cryptographic checksum (e.g., MD5 or SHA-256 hash) of the RAP file used to verify file integrity during transmission and ingestion. Supports non-repudiation and data quality assurance.
Physical size of the RAP file in bytes as received from the clearing house or sender operator. Used for file integrity validation and transmission monitoring.

business_glossary_term: Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange (NRTRDE) Flag
description: Indicates whether the rejected TAP records were originally subject to NRTRDE near-real-time roaming data exchange obligations. True if NRTRDE-governed records are included, enabling fraud and compliance monitoring.
reference: GSMA PRD FS.11 NRTRDE; GSMA BA.08; 3GPP TS 32.298

description: Free-text notes entered by the settlement operations team regarding this RAP file, such as root-cause analysis findings, escalation context, or correction instructions communicated to the counterparty operator.
reference: TM Forum eTOM; Amdocs Revenue Management

description: GSMA-standard primary rejection reason code identifying the main cause for TAP record rejection in this RAP file (e.g., '12' for missing mandatory field, '15' for invalid IMSI). Sourced from GSMA TD.32 rejection code table. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product — GSMA TD.32 defines 50+ rejection codes]
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; GSMA PRD TD.57

description: Date and time when the RAP file was fully processed and the rejected TAP records were actioned in the settlement system. Supports audit trail and SLA measurement.
reference: GSMA TD.32; Amdocs Revenue Management; TM Forum eTOM

business_glossary_term: Return of Accounting Procedure (RAP) File Type
description: GSMA-defined RAP file type code indicating the direction and nature of the rejection. HOMERJE = home operator rejecting visitor records; VISRJE = visited operator rejecting home records; ACK variants are acknowledgements; SYSERR = system error file. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HOMERJE|VISRJE|HOMERJE-ACK|VISRJE-ACK|SYSERR — promote to reference product]
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; GSMA PRD TD.57

business_glossary_term: Return of Accounting Procedure (RAP) Release Version
description: GSMA RAP release version within the specification version, providing finer-grained versioning of the RAP file format used for this exchange.

business_glossary_term: Return of Accounting Procedure (RAP) Specification Version
description: GSMA RAP specification version number used to encode this RAP file (e.g., '04' for RAP version 4). Governs the file structure and rejection code set applicable to this record.

business_glossary_term: Return of Accounting Procedure (RAP) File Status
description: Current lifecycle status of the RAP file within the inter-operator settlement workflow. Tracks progression from receipt through validation, processing, acknowledgement, and closure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: received|validated|processed|acknowledged|disputed|closed — promote to reference product]
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; TM Forum eTOM; Amdocs Revenue Management

description: Date and time when the RAP file was received and ingested by the recipient operator's settlement system. Used for SLA compliance tracking and NRTRDE window monitoring.
reference: GSMA TD.32; GSMA PRD BA.08; TM Forum SID

business_glossary_term: Recipient Transferred Account Data Interchange Group (TADIG) Code
description: GSMA TADIG code of the operator receiving this RAP file (the operator whose TAP records are being rejected). Identifies the counterparty in the bilateral exchange.
reference: GSMA PRD TD.57; GSMA TADIG Registry; GSMA BA.08

description: Timestamp when this RAP file record was first inserted into the Silver layer data product. Audit trail field for data lineage and lakehouse ingestion tracking.
Timestamp when this RAP file record was last modified in the Silver layer data product. Supports change data capture and audit trail requirements.
Total number of TAP CDR records rejected in this RAP file. Core settlement metric used to reconcile the volume of rejected usage records against the originating TAP file.
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; GSMA BA.08

description: GSMA-defined severity classification of the rejection: fatal (entire TAP file rejected), severe (significant errors requiring correction), or minor (non-critical errors). Determines the correction and resubmission workflow.
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; GSMA PRD TD.57

description: Pipe-delimited list of all GSMA rejection reason codes present across the rejected records in this RAP file. Provides a summary of all error types encountered, enabling root-cause analysis and TAP file correction prioritization.
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; GSMA PRD TD.57

description: Contractual or GSMA-mandated deadline by which the sender must resubmit corrected TAP records following this RAP rejection. Used for SLA monitoring and dispute escalation triggers.
reference: GSMA BA.08; GSMA TD.32; TM Forum SID

description: Current status of the TAP file resubmission process following this RAP rejection. Tracks whether the sender has corrected and resubmitted the rejected records, or if the rejection is under dispute or has been waived.
reference: GSMA TD.32; GSMA BA.08; TM Forum eTOM

description: Indicates whether the rejected TAP records relate to inbound roamers (foreign subscribers using the home network) or outbound roamers (home subscribers using a foreign network). Determines the financial flow direction for settlement.
reference: GSMA BA.08; GSMA PRD TD.57; TM Forum SID

business_glossary_term: Return of Accounting Procedure (RAP) File Sequence Number
description: GSMA-standard five-digit sequence number assigned to this RAP file by the sender, used to uniquely identify the RAP file within a bilateral exchange pair. Follows GSMA TD.32 sequencing rules.
reference: GSMA TD.32 RAP Format Specification; GSMA BA.08

description: Category of telecommunications service covered by the rejected TAP records (e.g., voice, data, SMS, MMS, supplementary services). Supports rejection analysis by service type for root-cause investigation.
reference: GSMA PRD TD.57; 3GPP TS 22.001; TM Forum SID

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the rejected charge amounts are denominated for inter-operator settlement (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Must align with the bilateral roaming agreement currency.
reference: ISO 4217; GSMA BA.08; ITU-T D.150; TM Forum SID

description: End date of the billing/settlement period covered by the rejected TAP records in this RAP file. Used with settlement_period_start_date to bound the financial exposure of the rejection.
reference: GSMA BA.08; ITU-T D.150; TM Forum SID

description: Start date of the billing/settlement period covered by the rejected TAP records in this RAP file. Aligns the rejection to the correct inter-operator settlement cycle.
reference: GSMA BA.08; ITU-T D.150; TM Forum SID

business_glossary_term: Source Transferred Account Procedure (TAP) File Sequence Number
description: The GSMA sequence number of the originating TAP file being rejected, as carried within the RAP file header. Enables direct correlation to the TAP file without requiring a system join.
TAP release version of the originating TAP file being rejected, providing finer-grained versioning within the TAP specification version. Used for format validation during RAP processing.
TAP specification version of the originating TAP file being rejected (e.g., '03' for TAP3). Required to validate that the RAP file is processed against the correct TAP format rules.

Aggregate monetary value of all TAP records rejected in this RAP file, expressed in the settlement currency. Represents the gross financial exposure of the rejection batch for inter-operator settlement reconciliation.
reference: GSMA TD.32; GSMA BA.08; ITU-T D.150; TM Forum SID

business_glossary_term: Total Tax Value of Rejected Records
description: Aggregate tax component of the rejected TAP records included in this RAP file. Required for accurate financial settlement reconciliation and tax reporting between operators.
reference: GSMA TD.32; GSMA BA.08; ITU-T D.150

description: GSMA-mandated cutoff timestamp by which the RAP file must be transmitted to the recipient operator. Used for SLA compliance monitoring and GSMA bilateral agreement enforcement.
reference: GSMA TD.32; GSMA BA.08; GSMA PRD TD.57

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the settlement dispute record in the interconnect domain. Primary key for this entity.

Foreign key linking to people.employee. Business justification: Interconnect disputes are manually investigated by revenue assurance analysts who validate TAP records, compare against IOT tariffs, and negotiate with carrier partners. Tracking the assigned analyst
Reference to the bilateral roaming or interconnect agreement under which the disputed settlement invoice or TAP file was generated.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.21; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Reference to the domestic or international carrier (counterparty) against whom the dispute is raised. Aligns with the PARTY_REFERENCE canonical category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA TAP/NRTRDE

description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Disputes are managed by specific operational teams (interconnect operations, revenue assurance). Cost allocation, resource planning, and operational efficiency tracking require knowing which cost cent
Reference to the IOT tariff table entry that Telecommunication believes should have been applied to the disputed charges. Central to rate_error and iot_mismatch dispute types.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.82; GSMA IOT Specification

description: Foreign key linking to partner.partner. Business justification: Interconnect settlement disputes may involve partners (MVNOs, wholesale customers) not just carriers. Business process: Partner dispute resolution workflow, escalation management, consolidated partner

Foreign key linking to analytics.pipeline_run. Business justification: Dispute records are created/updated via dispute management pipelines. This link supports audit trail for dispute lifecycle tracking, enables data quality monitoring of dispute processing, and tracks w

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_penalty. Business justification: Settlement disputes that escalate or involve regulatory violations may result in penalties (late settlement, fraudulent billing). Tracks penalty linkage for dispute escalation management and financial
Reference to the inter-operator settlement invoice that is the subject of this dispute. Null when the dispute is raised directly against a TAP file rather than a consolidated invoice.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA TAP3 Specification

description: Reference to the specific TAP file whose charges are disputed. Null when the dispute is raised at the consolidated invoice level rather than at the individual TAP file level.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification; GSMA PRD TD.57

description: Foreign key linking to assurance.trouble_ticket. Business justification: Settlement disputes requiring technical investigation (TAP file discrepancies, rating errors, network issues) generate trouble tickets. Critical for dispute resolution workflow linking commercial and

Portion of the original invoice or TAP file charge that Telecommunication accepts as valid and agrees to pay. The difference between the invoiced amount and the disputed amount. Part of MONETARY_TRIPLET canonical category (adjustment component).
reference: GSMA PRD IR.82; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Date on which the counterparty carrier formally responded to the dispute notification. Used to measure SLA compliance and track negotiation progress.
Free-text summary of the carrier's formal response to the dispute, including their position, counter-evidence references, and proposed resolution.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.82; TM Forum SID GB922

description: Reference number of the credit note issued by the carrier as part of the dispute resolution. Populated when resolution_type is credit_note or partial_credit.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.82; Amdocs Revenue Management

description: High-level grouping of the dispute: financial (monetary discrepancy), technical (CDR or TAP file format/content issue), or contractual (disagreement on agreement terms or IOT applicability).
reference: TM Forum SID GB922; GSMA PRD IR.82

description: Free-text narrative describing the nature of the dispute, the specific charges contested, and the business justification for the claim. Authored by the settlement analyst at the time of dispute creation.

Indicates whether Telecommunication is the disputing party (outbound — Telecommunication raises dispute against carrier) or the receiving party (inbound — carrier raises dispute against Telecommunication).
reference: GSMA PRD IR.82; TM Forum SID GB922

description: The applicable tax rate (as a percentage) used to calculate the tax_amount for this settlement line item. Determined by the tax jurisdiction and service type.
reference: TM Forum SID GB922 — Tax Rate; IFRS 15; ISO 3166-1

description: Classification of the traffic flow direction and type for this settlement line. Distinguishes inbound roaming (MVNO/visited network charges), outbound roaming, transit traffic, and wholesale termination for revenue assurance and regulatory reporting.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.21; TM Forum eTOM — Interconnect Management; FCC Interconnection Rules

description: Total quantity of traffic units (calls, messages, data bytes, or events) included in this settlement line item. The unit of measure is defined by traffic_volume_unit.

business_glossary_term: Visited Network Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) Code
description: The PLMN code (MCC+MNC) of the visited network where the roaming service was consumed. Used in TAP3 reconciliation and IOT tariff application for inbound/outbound roaming settlement.
reference: ITU-T E.212 — PLMN Identification; 3GPP TS 23.003; GSMA TAP3 TD.57

reference: TM Forum SID; GSMA TAP3 Specification

The date and time at which the recipient operator or clearinghouse issued a formal acknowledgement (RAP or positive ACK) for this TAP file. Marks the completion of the file exchange lifecycle for settlement purposes.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA RAP Specification TD.32

description: The name of the inter-operator clearinghouse or data exchange hub through which this TAP file was routed (e.g., Syniverse, BICS, GSMA Clearing House). Identifies the intermediary responsible for file routing, validation, and settlement statement generation.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA Clearing House Procedures

description: The unique reference number assigned by the inter-operator clearinghouse (e.g., GSMA Clearing House, Syniverse, BICS) upon receipt of this TAP file. Used for end-to-end traceability, dispute resolution, and reconciliation against clearinghouse settlement statements.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA Clearing House Procedures

description: The date and time at which this TAP file record was first captured in the interconnect settlement data platform (Silver layer). Audit trail field for data lineage and reconciliation.

The timestamp of the latest CDR event contained within this TAP file, representing the end of the usage data period covered by the batch. Used alongside data_period_start_timestamp for gap detection and completeness validation.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA PRD TD.32

description: The timestamp of the earliest CDR event contained within this TAP file, representing the start of the usage data period covered by the batch. Used for period-based reconciliation, billing cycle alignment, and regulatory reporting.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA PRD TD.32

description: The reference number of any commercial dispute raised against this TAP file by the recipient operator or clearinghouse. Populated when file_status is 'disputed'. Links to the dispute management workflow for IOT charge challenges and resolution tracking.
reference: GSMA PRD BA.12; TM Forum eTOM; GSMA TAP3 TD.57

description: The foreign exchange rate applied to convert the TAP file settlement currency to the home operator's local accounting currency at the time of settlement. Used for financial reporting, revenue assurance, and EBITDA calculations in multi-currency environments.
reference: GSMA PRD BA.12; ISO 4217; SAP S/4HANA Finance Module

description: The date and time at which the TAP file was generated by the sending operator's mediation or billing system (Amdocs Revenue Management). Represents the principal business event time for the file batch. Used for timeliness SLA measurement per GSMA NRTRDE and TAP submission deadlines.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA NRTRDE Specification

description: The physical size of the TAP file in bytes as received from the sender or clearinghouse. Used for transmission integrity checks, storage capacity planning, and anomaly detection (unusually large or small files may indicate encoding errors).

Current lifecycle state of the TAP file within the inter-operator settlement workflow. Transitions: created → sent → acknowledged (clean acceptance) or rejected (validation failure) → disputed (commercial challenge) or resubmitted (corrected re-send). Drives settlement reconciliation and SLA monitoring.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; TM Forum eTOM Process Framework

description: Classifies the type of inter-operator data exchange file: TAP (standard Transferred Account Procedure batch), NRTRDE (Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange for fraud detection), RAP (Returned Account Procedure for rejected records), or STOP (Stop file halting processing). Determines processing pipeline and settlement treatment.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA NRTRDE Specification PRD TD.32

description: The version identifier of the Inter-Operator Tariff (IOT) schedule applied to rate the CDRs in this TAP file. Ensures the correct tariff table is used for settlement validation and dispute resolution when tariff changes occur mid-period.
reference: GSMA IOT Specification PRD BA.12; GSMA TAP3 TD.57

description: Indicates whether this TAP file is a test/simulation file (True) or a live production file (False) carrying real roaming charges. Test files must be excluded from financial settlement calculations and revenue reporting.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA PRD TD.32

description: The predominant radio access network technology type of the CDRs contained in this TAP file (e.g., LTE, 5G NR, VoLTE). Used for technology-segmented roaming analytics, IOT tariff differentiation, and network capacity planning.
reference: 3GPP TS 32.297; GSMA TAP3 TD.57; ETSI TS 132 297

business_glossary_term: Near Real-Time Roaming Data Exchange (NRTRDE) Reference
description: The reference identifier linking this TAP file to its corresponding NRTRDE near-real-time roaming data exchange record. NRTRDE files are transmitted within 4 hours of call completion for fraud detection; this reference enables correlation between the NRTRDE early notification and the final TAP settlement file.
reference: GSMA NRTRDE Specification PRD TD.32; GSMA TAP3 TD.57

description: For resubmitted TAP files, the sequence number of the original file that this resubmission replaces. Enables lineage tracing from corrected files back to the original rejected batch. Null for first-time submissions.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA RAP Specification TD.32

description: The outcome of the TAP file processing pipeline within the operator's BSS/OSS systems (Amdocs Revenue Management, Netcracker OSS/BSS). Indicates whether all CDRs were successfully rated and posted to settlement accounts, partially processed, or failed. Drives exception management workflows.
reference: TM Forum eTOM; GSMA TAP3 TD.57; Amdocs Revenue Management

description: The reference number of the RAP (Returned Account Procedure) file generated in response to validation failures in this TAP file. Links the TAP file to its corresponding rejection notification for dispute tracking and resubmission management.
reference: GSMA RAP Specification TD.32; GSMA TAP3 TD.57

description: The date and time at which the TAP file was received and acknowledged at the clearinghouse or by the recipient operator. Used to calculate transit latency and confirm delivery within bilateral SLA windows.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA PRD TD.32

description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the recipient operator's home country. Used for bilateral traffic analysis, regulatory reporting, and determining applicable IOT tariff zones and settlement currency conventions.
reference: ISO 3166-1; GSMA TAP3 TD.57; ITU-T E.212

description: The five-character TADIG code identifying the receiving (home) network operator to whom this TAP file is addressed. Determines routing through the clearinghouse and the settlement counterparty for IOT charges.
reference: GSMA TADIG Code Registry; GSMA TAP3 TD.57

description: The reconciliation state of this TAP file against the clearinghouse settlement statement. Tracks whether the file's declared charges match the clearinghouse-confirmed amounts. Discrepancies trigger revenue assurance investigations. Used for MRR and ARPU reporting accuracy.
reference: TM Forum eTOM; GSMA Clearing House Procedures; GSMA PRD BA.12

description: The number of times this TAP file has been resubmitted after rejection or dispute. A value greater than zero indicates the file has been corrected and resent. Used for operator performance monitoring and SLA compliance tracking.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA RAP Specification TD.32

description: Indicates whether this TAP file represents inbound roaming (foreign subscribers using our network — we are the visited operator and sender) or outbound roaming (our subscribers using a foreign network — we are the home operator and recipient). Critical for revenue assurance and IOT settlement accounting.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; TM Forum eTOM; GSMA PRD BA.12

description: The sequential file number assigned by the sending operator to uniquely identify this TAP file within the bilateral exchange. Follows GSMA TAP3 five-digit sequence numbering convention (00001–99999, wrapping). Used for duplicate detection and gap analysis in file receipt tracking.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification TD.57; ITU-T E.212

description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the TAP file charges are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Governs the currency for clearinghouse settlement and financial reconciliation between operators.
reference: ISO 4217; GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA PRD BA.12

description: The reference number of the clearinghouse settlement statement that includes charges from this TAP file. Links the TAP file batch to the financial settlement document used for inter-operator payment and accounting entries in SAP S/4HANA.
reference: GSMA Clearing House Procedures; SAP S/4HANA Finance Module; GSMA PRD BA.12

description: The name of the operational system of record that generated or ingested this TAP file record (e.g., Amdocs Revenue Management, Comverse ONE, Netcracker OSS/BSS). Used for data lineage tracking and issue triage in the Silver layer.

The date and time at which the TAP file was submitted to the clearinghouse or directly to the recipient operator. Used to measure compliance with GSMA TAP submission timeliness requirements (typically within 36 hours of the last CDR in the file).
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA PRD TD.32

description: The TAP3 protocol release version used to encode this file (e.g., TAP3R10, TAP3R12). Governs the ASN.1 schema and field set applicable to the file. Critical for parser selection during file ingestion and validation.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification TD.57; ETSI TS 132 297

description: The total tax component included in the TAP file charge amount, as declared in the file header. Applicable in jurisdictions where VAT or withholding tax applies to inter-operator roaming settlements. Used for financial reporting and tax compliance.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA PRD BA.12; FCC Regulatory Reporting

description: The total number of Call Detail Records (CDRs) contained within this TAP file as declared in the file header. Used for completeness validation against the actual parsed record count and for settlement volume reporting.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; TM Forum SID

description: The gross total Inter-Operator Tariff (IOT) charge amount declared in the TAP file header, representing the sum of all roaming charges for CDRs in this batch. Expressed in the settlement currency. Used as the primary financial control total for clearinghouse reconciliation and operator settlement.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA IOT Specification PRD BA.12

description: The date and time at which this TAP file record was most recently modified in the interconnect settlement data platform. Tracks status transitions, validation updates, and reconciliation changes.

The total number of validation errors identified during TAP file parsing and structural/business rule validation. A non-zero value triggers RAP (Returned Account Procedure) generation. Used for quality monitoring and operator performance tracking.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA RAP Specification

description: A structured summary of the validation errors encountered during TAP file processing, including error codes and descriptions as defined in the GSMA TAP3 specification. Supports root cause analysis, operator dispute resolution, and resubmission guidance.
reference: GSMA TAP3 TD.57; GSMA RAP Specification TD.32

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each individual TAP roaming usage record (CDR) within the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for the tap_record data product.
reference: GSMA TAP3 Specification (TD.57); TM Forum SID

description: Reference to the bilateral roaming agreement governing this inter-operator traffic exchange, linking to the applicable IOT tariff and settlement terms.
reference: GSMA PRD IR.21; TM Forum SID

description: Identifier of the radio cell or base station where the roaming subscriber was served during this event, as reported by the visited network. Used for geographic traffic analysis and network capacity planning.

E.164 telephone number of the called party (B-number) for MOC voice events. Used for traffic analysis, fraud detection (e.g., IRSF detection), and regulatory reporting. Null for MTC, GPRS, and messaging events.
